questions.q: What did King David tell his son Solomon?
questions.a: David told his son to obey everything that God directed and instructed them to do.

questions.q: What was Yahweh’s promise to David?
questions.a: Yahweh promised that David would never cease to have a descendant on Israel’s throne.

questions.q: What did King David’s tell Solomon about Joab, the son of Zeruiah?
questions.a: King David told Solomon not to let him die peacefully.

questions.q: What had the sons of Barzillai done for King David?
questions.a: The sons of Barzillai had given David food and drink when he fled from Absalom.

questions.q: What had Shimei done to King David?
questions.a: Shimei had violently cursed King David.

questions.q: What did Kind David tell Solomon to do to Shimei?
questions.a: David told Solomon not to let Shimei go free from punishment, but to bring him down to the grave with blood.

questions.q: How long did King David reign over Israel?
questions.a: David reigned for 40 years.

questions.q: What did Adonijah say to Bathsheba when he came to her?
questions.a: Adonijah said that all Israel expected him to be King but Yahweh gave it to his brother Solomon.

questions.q: What did Adonijah request from Bathsheba?
questions.a: Adonijah requested that she ask Solomon for Abishag the Shunammite to be given to him as his wife.

questions.q: Why did Bathsheba go to Solomon?
questions.a: Bathsheba went to Solomon to ask that Abishag would be given to Adonijah as his wife.

questions.q: What did King Solomon say in response to Bathsheba?
questions.a: Solomon said that Adonijah had spoken this request at the cost of his life.

questions.q: Who did King Solomon send to execute Adonijah?
questions.a: Solomon sent Benaiah son of Jehoiada to execute Adonijah.

questions.q: What did King Solomon tell Abiathar the priest to do?
questions.a: Solomon told Abiathar to go back to his fields and dismissed him from being priest.

questions.q: Where did Joab go to flee from Solomon?
questions.a: Joab fled to the tent of Yahweh and took hold of the horns of the altar.

questions.q: What did King Solomon send Benaiah son of Jehoiada to do?
questions.a: Solomon sent him to kill Joab.

questions.q: What did Joab say to Benaiah the son of Jehoiada?
questions.a: Joab told him that he would not come out of the temple and would die at the altar.

questions.q: What did King Solomon tell Benaiah to do to Joab?
questions.a: Solomon told Benaiah to do as Joab had said.

questions.q: Why did King Solomon want Joab to be killed?
questions.a: Solomon wanted Joab to be killed because Joab murdered two righteous men, Abner, commander of the army of Israel, and Amasa, the commander of the army of Judah, without King David knowing about it.

questions.q: What did King Solomon do to reward Benaiah son of Jehoiada?
questions.a: Solomon put him in charge of the army in place of Joab.

questions.q: Where did King Solomon allow Shimei to live?
questions.a: Solomon told Shimei that he could live in Jerusalem.

questions.q: What warning did King Solomon give to Shimei when he allowed him to live in Jerusalem?
questions.a: Solomon told Shimei that if he left Jerusalem to go any other place, he would die.

questions.q: Why did Shimei saddle his donkey and leave Jerusalem to go to Gath?
questions.a: Shimei went to Gath to bring back two of his servants who had run away from him.

questions.q: What did King Solomon say that Shimei had done to Yahweh?
questions.a: Solomon told Shimei that he had not kept his oath to Yahweh, and that Yahweh would return his evil back on his own head.

questions.q: What did King Solomon do when he was told that Shimei had left Jerusalem?
questions.a: Solomon told Benaiah the son of Jehoiada to put Shimei to death.

commentary.text: David's charge as to Joab and others.
Solomon reigns, Adonijah aspiring to the throne is put to death.
Abiathar banished, Joab put to death.

Verses 1–4 David's charge to Solomon is, to keep the charge of the Lord. The authority of a dying father is much, but nothing to that of a living God. God promised David that the Messiah should come from his descendants, and that promise was absolute; but the promise, that there should not fail of them a man on the throne of Israel, was conditional; if he walks before God in sincerity, with zeal and resolution: in order hereunto, he must take heed to his way. (1Ki 2:5-11)

These dying counsels concerning Joab and Shimei, did not come from personal anger, but for the security of Solomon's throne, which was the murders he had committed, but would readily repeat them to carry any purpose; though long reprieved, he shall be reckoned with at last. Time does not wear out the guilt of any sin, particularly of murder. Concerning Shimei, Hold him not guiltless; do not think him any true friend to thee, or thy government, or fit to be trusted; he has no less malice now than he had then. David's dying sentiments are recorded, as delivered under the influence of the Holy Ghost, 2Sa 23:1–7. The Lord discovered to him the offices and the salvation of that glorious personage, the Messiah, whose coming he then foretold, and from whom he derived all his comforts and expectations. That passage gives a decided proof that David died under the influence of the Holy Ghost, in the exercise of faith and hope.

Solomon received Bathsheba with all the respect that was owing to a mother; but let none be asked for that which they ought not to grant. It ill becomes a good man to prefer a bad request, or to appear in a bad cause. According to eastern customs it was plain that Adonijah sought to be king, by his asking for Abishag as his wife, and Solomon could not be safe while he lived. Ambitious, turbulent spirits commonly prepare death for themselves. Many a head has been lost by catching at a crown.

Solomon's words to Abiathar, and his silence, imply that some recent conspiracies had been entered into. Those that show kindness to God's people shall have it remembered to their advantage. For this reason Solomon spares Abiathar's life, but dismisses him from his offices. In case of such sins as the blood of beasts would atone for, the altar was a refuge, but not in Joab's case. Solomon looks upward to God as the Author of peace, and forward to eternity as the perfection of it. The Lord of peace himself gives us that peace which is everlasting.

The old malignity remains in the unconverted heart, and a watchful eye should be kept on those who, like Shimei, have manifested their enmity, but have given no evidence of repentance. No engagements or dangers will restrain worldly men; they go on, though they forfeit their lives and souls. Let us remember, God will not accommodate his judgment to us. His eye is over us; and let us strive to walk as in his presence. Let our every act, word, and thought, be governed by this great truth, that the hour is quickly coming when the smallest circumstances of our lives shall be brought to light, and our eternal state be fixed by a righteous and unerring God. Thus Solomon's throne was established in peace, as the type of the Redeemer's kingdom of peace and righteousness. And it is a comfort, in reference to the enmity of the church's enemies, that, how much soever they rage, it is a vain thing they imagine. Christ's throne is established, and they cannot shake it.
